extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and U.S. Patent Office examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing computation of reply periods, shortened statutory periods and specified time limits, handling of inadvertent omissions in replies, and procedures/limits for obtaining extensions of time in U.S. patent prosecution (37 CFR 1.135, 1.136 and related MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after final rejection do not save from abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal to admit, any amendment after final rejection, or any related proceedings, will not operate to save the application from abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any admission of, or refusal to admit, amendment not responsive to the last action, or related proceedings, will not operate to save the application from abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of bona fide but substantially complete replies with inadvertent omissions (37 CFR 1.135(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may accept a reply to a non-final Office action that is bona fide and is substantially complete but for an inadvertent omission as an adequate reply to avoid abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 133 and 37 CFR 1.135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of omissions that may be corrected under this practice include an amendment unsigned or improperly signed, or an amendment presenting additional claims requiring additional fees. Examiner may give a shortened statutory time period (generally 1 month) to correct the omission (e.g., provide duplicate paper or submit fees or cancel claims). Failure to timely supply the omission will result in abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 133 and 37 CFR 1.135. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b) will be available unless the Office action indicates otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omissions that do not preclude action on the merits may be waived
rubrics_metrics.description: When a bona fide attempt to reply includes an omission that does not preclude action on the merits (e.g., a reply fails to address a rejection or objection), the examiner may waive the deficiency and act on the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options available to the examiner include: (A) issuing an Office action that does not treat the reply on its merits but requires the applicant to supply the omission to avoid abandonment; or (B) issuing an Office action that does treat the reply on its merits. The examiner may also repeat and make final the rejection, objection, or requirement that was the subject of the omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner discretion and abuse of 1.135(c) protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to provide a 1-month shortened statutory time period to supply an omission is within the examiner's discretion; examiner determines whether the omission was inadvertent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner determines the omission was not inadvertent (e.g., applicant is abusing 37 CFR 1.135(c) to gain time or delay examination), the examiner should notify the applicant of the omission and advise that it must be supplied within the period for reply to the prior action, including extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a), if permitted. See MPEP § 714.03 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of statutory period for reply
rubrics_metrics.description: The actual time taken for reply is computed from the date stamped or printed on the Office action to the date of receipt by the Office of applicant’s reply; no cognizance is taken of fractions of a day and applicant’s reply is due on the corresponding day of the month specified after the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: reply to an Office action with a 3-month shortened statutory period dated November 30 is due on the following February 28 (or 29 if leap year). A 1-month extension moves the due date to the corresponding day (e.g., Jan 31 -> April 30; with 1-month extension -> May 31). The Office 'date' stamp on the reply paper is the date of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failing to file a timely reply (abandonment)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a timely reply is ultimately not filed, the application is regarded as abandoned after midnight of the date the period for reply expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fact that the following day may be a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday does not change the abandonment date. See MPEP § 711.04 regarding handling of abandoned applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-day period and weekend/holiday rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A 30-day period for reply in the Office means 30 calendar days including Saturdays, Sundays, and federal holidays; however, if the period ends on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday, filing on the next succeeding business day is timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the period for reply is extended, the time extended is added to the last calendar day of the original period, not to a shifted business day. The Office date stamp determines the date of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office date stamp determines date of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of receipt of a reply to an Office action is given by the 'Office date' stamp which appears on the reply paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure timely filing so the Office date stamp reflects receipt within the period for reply or any granted extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory periods: minimum and common durations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 133 and 37 CFR 1.136 an applicant may be required to reply in a shorter period than 6 months, not less than 30 days. The length of the shortened statutory period depends on the type of reply required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific examples provided: minimum not less than 30 days (35 U.S.C. 133); (1) 30 days for submitting an oath or declaration in compliance with § 1.63; (2) 1 month (not less than 30 days) for submitting formal drawings under § 1.85(c); (3) period for making a deposit under § 1.809(c). Other situational periods: 1 month for bona fide reply with inadvertent omission (MPEP §§ 710.01 & 714.03); 2 months for winning party in terminated interference to reply to an unanswered Office action and to reply to an Ex parte Quayle Office action; 3 months to reply to any Office action on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit actions (specified time limits) and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: There are situations where the examiner specifies a time limit for an applicant to take some action and failure to timely take that action results in a consequence other than abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) petition under 37 CFR 1.14(a) for public access — usually 3 weeks to state objections; failure does not affect prosecution but Office decides without applicant's objections (MPEP § 103). (B) IDS incomplete — examiner may set a 1-month time limit to complete IDS; failure does not cause abandonment but the omitted info is placed in file and not considered (MPEP § 609.05(a)). (C) Where application is otherwise allowable but contains a traverse of restriction requirement, applicant may be given a specified time (e.g., 1-month) to cancel claims to non-elected invention; failure treated as authorization to cancel and application passed to issue (see 37 CFR 1.141, 1.144 and MPEP § 821). (D) Examiner may require applicant to add claim to provoke interference; failure to satisfy within period (not less than 1 month) operates as a concession of priority — not abandonment (MPEP Chapter 2300).

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between shortened statutory periods and specified time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Shortened statutory periods (set under 35 U.S.C. 133) and specified time limits are distinct and carry different penalties and extension rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties: (A) Failure to meet a specified time results in loss of rights regarding that particular matter (e.g., concession of priority), but not abandonment of the entire application. (B) Failure to reply within a shortened statutory period results in abandonment of the entire application and is not appealable (though petition to revive may be available under 37 CFR 1.137). (C) A specified time may be set for less than the 30-day minimum applicable to statutory periods. (D) Examiners may excuse small delays for specified time limits with satisfactory explanation; even a 1-2 day late reply in a statutory period results in abandonment. Appeal brief time periods (37 CFR 41.37) are not statutory periods under 35 U.S.C. 133 and are typically extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a) unless otherwise provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restarting the period for reply when Office action is defective
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the citation of a reference is incorrect or an Office action contains some other defect and this error is called to the Office's attention within 1 month of the mail date, the Office will restart the previously set period for reply to run from the date the error is corrected, if requested by applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 710.06 for procedure; applicant must call the defect to the Office's attention within 1 month of mailing to obtain restart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a): petition & fee up to 5 months
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is required to reply within a nonstatutory or shortened statutory time period, applicant may extend the time period for reply up to the earlier of the expiration of any maximum period set by statute or five months after the time period set for reply if a petition and the fee set in § 1.17(a) are filed, unless exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions where 1.136(a) extension and fee are not available are listed (i) applicant notified otherwise in Office action; (ii) reply is a reply brief under § 41.41; (iii) reply is a request for oral hearing under § 41.47(a); (iv) reply to Board decision per § 1.304 or § 41.50/41.52; (v) application involved in a contested case (§ 41.101(a)). The date the petition and fee are filed is used to determine the period of extension and the corresponding fee amount. A reply must be filed prior to expiration of the period of extension to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3) constructive petitions and fee authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: A written request in an application may authorize treating any concurrent or future reply requiring a petition for extension as incorporating a petition for extension; authorization to charge fees or submission of the extension fee will be treated as a constructive petition for an extension of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three constructive mechanisms: (A) prior written request to treat a reply as incorporating petition; (B) prior authorization to charge required fees (or extension fees) to a deposit account; (C) submission of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(a) with the reply. Office recommends including a written petition in reply to avoid processing delays; sample petition text provided in MPEP. Constructive petitions provide a 'safety net' to avoid inadvertent loss of rights where petition was omitted but fee/authorization present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(b) require sufficient cause and timely filing
rubrics_metrics.description: When 1.136(a) is not available, the period for reply may be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified; any request must be filed on or before the day the reply is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere filing of a request under 1.136(b) does not itself affect an extension; a request must be accompanied by the petition fee under 1.17(g). No extension under 1.136(b) may carry the due date beyond the statutory maximum period. Extensions under 1.136(b) must state a reason in support and will only be granted for sufficient cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific time periods not extendable after Notice of Allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is notified in a 'Notice of Allowability' that an application is otherwise in condition for allowance, certain time periods are not extendable if set in the Notice or in an Office action having a mail date on or after the Notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-extendable periods include: (1) period for submitting an oath or declaration in compliance with § 1.63; (2) period for submitting formal drawings under § 1.85(c); (3) period for making a deposit under § 1.809(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and limited situations where 1.136(a) is inapplicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions with payment of a fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not available in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of exceptions: (A) all extensions in a reexamination proceeding (see 37 CFR 1.550(c) and MPEP § 2265 for ex parte reexamination and 37 CFR 1.956/MPEP § 2665 for inter partes); (B) all extensions during an interference proceeding (but not preparatory proceedings where a claim is suggested for interference); (C) specific Office actions stating 37 CFR 1.136(a) is not applicable (e.g., reply to notice of allowability, reissue applications associated with litigation, applications in allowable condition with nonelected claims where time is set to cancel such claims); (D) limited instances where applicant is given a specified time limit to take certain actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for extensions are cumulative and subject to small entity reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees for extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(a) and are cumulative; small entities qualify for a 50% reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant paid a 1-month extension fee and later needs another month, the proper fee is the amount for the 2-month extension less the amount previously paid for 1 month. Fee calculations are cumulative and must be matched to the amount of extension requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice treating late petitions with fee authorization as requesting appropriate extension
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition (and requisite fee) requesting an insufficient period of extension is filed such that the petition would be filed outside the so-extended period, but the period could be further extended under 1.136(a) and the petition/application contains an authorization to charge extension fees or fees under 37 CFR 1.17, Office practice is to treat the petition as requesting the period necessary to make the petition filed within the further extended period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a petition for a two-month extension filed 4.5 months after the date of notice of appeal may be treated as requesting three months (the period necessary) if fee authorization exists. This practice applies even if no further reply is filed; the petition is construed as requesting the appropriate period when fee authorization or deposit account charging is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for petitions in continuing applications and effect on prior application
rubrics_metrics.description: To facilitate processing, any petition for an extension of time (or petition to revive) in which a continuing application is filed in lieu of a reply should explicitly refer to the filing of the continuing application and include an express abandonment of the prior application conditioned upon granting of the petition and a filing date to the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are cautioned that filing a petition or fee authorization in the continuing application does not effect an extension in the prior application; petitions must be filed in the application to which they pertain per 37 CFR 1.4 and 1.5. Ensure petitions are filed in the correct application to obtain the intended extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority limits: examiner/Director cannot extend shortened statutory period absent petition; no extension beyond 6 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the primary examiner nor the Director of the USPTO has authority to extend a shortened statutory period unless a petition for extension is filed; no extension can extend the time beyond the six-month statutory period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the shortened period may be extended within the statutory 6 months, extensions cannot operate to extend beyond the 6-month maximum. Petitions under 1.136(a) must be filed within the extended period for reply; 1.136(b) requests must be filed prior to end of set period for reply.
